outcome.answer: Yes — the closest matches are papers on lifecycle memory control and strength-like memory management. [1] explicitly introduces strength as a lifecycle state for retention consequence and frames memory as a lifecycle-control problem. [8] also has a complete memory lifecycle with explicit strength and evidence tracking, but it is for recommendation and uses event, preference, and profile tiers. [2], [7], and [9] focus more on forgetting, reconsolidation, or consolidation control than on lifecycle strength specifically.
